account: Ruocco, Amenta, Angeloni, Frisicale, Vaia and Sagaro reported a case in International Maritime Health (2025;76(2):93–96). The early publication date is 5 March 2025 as printed on the journal page. They are at the University of Camerino's Telemedicine and Telepharmacy Center, the Centro Internazionale Radio Medico (CIRM) research department and Italy's Ministry of Health. A 43-year-old chief officer from the United Kingdom fell ill on a merchant ship in the middle of the Indian Ocean. He had chest pain, malaise and palpitations. CIRM, the Italian Telemedical Maritime Assistance Service, received the request on 29 September 2023. Blood pressure was 115/80 then 110/70 mmHg with tachycardia and an irregular heartbeat. The ship had no electrocardiograph and was too far from land for prompt rescue. The captain and the CIRM duty doctor used a smartwatch's electrocardiogram (ECG) application. Within seconds it confirmed the diagnostic hypothesis of atrial fibrillation (AF). The doctor reviewed the recording and recommended diversion to the nearest port. Metoprolol 100 mg and aspirin 300 mg daily were given on board. The hospital later confirmed AF. The seafarer, with no prior history, was repatriated safely without complications and diagnosed with new-onset AF. The report does not name the watch's brand or whose watch it was.

ai_role.statement: The smartwatch supplied an ECG that the CIRM physician interpreted as atrial fibrillation. The authors say that the app confirmed the hypothesis within seconds, which makes an automatic AF flag plausible, but they do not identify the device or distinguish an algorithmic classification from the physician’s reading. Diversion, treatment and hospital confirmation were human decisions.

fields.account: Ruocco, Amenta, Angeloni, Frisicale, Vaia and Sagaro reported a case in International Maritime Health (2025;76(2):93–96). The early publication date is 5 March 2025 as printed on the journal page. They are at the University of Camerino's Telemedicine and Telepharmacy Center, the Centro Internazionale Radio Medico (CIRM) research department and Italy's Ministry of Health. A 43-year-old chief officer from the United Kingdom fell ill on a merchant ship in the middle of the Indian Ocean. He had chest pain, malaise and palpitations. CIRM, the Italian Telemedical Maritime Assistance Service, received the request on 29 September 2023. Blood pressure was 115/80 then 110/70 mmHg with tachycardia and an irregular heartbeat. The ship had no electrocardiograph and was too far from land for prompt rescue. The captain and the CIRM duty doctor used a smartwatch's electrocardiogram (ECG) application. Within seconds it confirmed the diagnostic hypothesis of atrial fibrillation (AF). The doctor reviewed the recording and recommended diversion to the nearest port. Metoprolol 100 mg and aspirin 300 mg daily were given on board. The hospital later confirmed AF. The seafarer, with no prior history, was repatriated safely without complications and diagnosed with new-onset AF. The report does not name the watch's brand or whose watch it was.
